blocks.h: Life Insurance in Nigeria: A Professional Body of Knowledge

This appendix contains five specimen insurance documents, each accompanied by annotation notes explaining the function, regulatory basis, and practical significance of key provisions. These documents are for educational and professional reference purposes. They are not legally binding instruments and must not be used as actual policy documents, proposal forms, or quotations without adaptation by qualified legal and actuarial professionals.
• Document 2A: Individual Term Life Assurance Policy — Specimen (Annotated)
• Document 2B: Life Assurance Proposal Form with Guidance Notes
• Document 2C: Group Life Insurance Master Policy — Selected Clauses (Annotated)
• Document 2D: Retirement Life Annuity Quotation Template
• Document 2E: Life Insurance Claims Notification Form

All documents in this appendix are specimen templates for educational purposes only. Company names, policy numbers, and any personal details shown are fictitious. No reliance should be placed on these documents in any commercial, legal, or regulatory context. Actual insurance policies, proposal forms, and quotations used with policyholders must be: (1) approved by NAICOM under the product approval process required by NIIRA 2025; (2) reviewed by qualified legal counsel; (3) actuarially certified where required. The annotation notes in this appendix are provided to illuminate the purpose and regulatory basis of each document clause — they form part of the educational text of this book, not part of any insurance contract.

blocks.h: The Policy Schedule is the personalised part of the policy — it contains the specific details that distinguish this policy from every other. Together with the Policy Conditions (below), it forms the complete insurance contract. Key points:
• NAICOM Product Approval Reference: All life insurance products must be approved by NAICOM before marketing. The approval reference confirms the product’s regulatory standing. [Chapter 21]

• Nominated Beneficiary: The person entitled to receive the death benefit. Under AIICO Insurance Plc v. Benson (2014), the policy nomination overrides a conflicting instruction in the policyholder’s will. The nomination should be reviewed after life events (marriage, divorce, birth of children). [Chapters 12, 25]

• Grace Period: Most Nigerian life policies allow a grace period of 30 days (15 days for monthly premiums) for premium payment before a policy lapses; the period is set by the policy conditions and is not a minimum fixed by NIIRA 2025. During the grace period, the policy remains in force and a claim would be payable (though the outstanding premium would be deducted from any benefit). [Chapter 11]
OPERATIVE CLAUSE

APEX LIFE INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (hereinafter “the Company”) agrees, in consideration of the payment of the premium set out in the Policy Schedule and in reliance on the statements made in the Proposal Form dated 28 July 2025 (which form the basis of this contract), to pay the Sum Assured specified in the Policy Schedule to the nominated beneficiary or the legal representative of the Life Assured upon the occurrence of the Death of the Life Assured during the Policy Term, provided that:

items.h: All premiums due have been paid and no premium is outstanding beyond the Grace Period at the date of death;
The death does not arise from an Excluded Cause as set out in the Exclusions clause of this Policy; and
The claim is notified to the Company within twelve (12) months of the date of death, accompanied by the documents specified in the Claims Procedure clause.

blocks.h: The operative clause is the insurer’s primary contractual promise. It creates the enforceable obligation to pay. Note the three provisos: premium payment, no exclusion, and timely notification. The doctrine of utmost good faith means the insurer’s promise is conditional on the accuracy of the proposal form (‘in reliance on the statements made’). A material misrepresentation in the proposal form can void the policy. [Chapters 11, 12; Adesanya v. Royal Exchange (1986)]
DEFINITIONS

rows: The cessation of all biological functions of the Life Assured, certified by a registered medical practitioner and evidenced by a Certificate of Death issued by a competent authority in Nigeria or, where death occurs outside Nigeria, by the equivalent authority in the relevant jurisdiction.

The period of thirty (30) days following the due date of each premium during which the premium may be paid without the Policy lapsing. The Policy remains in force during the Grace Period, but the Company may deduct any outstanding premium from any benefit payable.
The termination of this Policy by reason of non-payment of a premium within the Grace Period. A lapsed Policy provides no benefit unless reinstated in accordance with the Reinstatement condition.
The application completed by the Policyholder dated 28 July 2025, together with any supplementary questionnaires and medical evidence provided to the Company before this Policy was issued.
The period from the Commencement Date to the Expiry Date as specified in the Policy Schedule, being twenty (20) years.

Any cause of death described in the Exclusions clause of this Policy.

blocks.h: POLICY CONDITIONS
1. Payment of Premium

The premium specified in the Policy Schedule shall be paid by the Policyholder to the Company on or before the due date in each period. Payment may be made by direct debit, electronic funds transfer, mobile money, or any other method approved by the Company in writing. The Company shall issue a receipt for each premium payment, which shall constitute evidence of payment. Payment to an agent shall not be deemed payment to the Company, because an insurance agent may not collect premium (s.38(2) NIIRA 2025). Premium collected by a licensed broker is deemed paid to the Company (s.60(2) NIIRA 2025).
2. Free Look Period

The Policyholder has the right to cancel this Policy within twenty-one (21) days of the date of receipt of the Policy document (the ‘Free Look Period’) by returning the Policy document to the Company’s registered office with a written notice of cancellation. Upon receipt of a valid cancellation notice within the Free Look Period, the Company shall refund the full premium paid without deduction. No claim may be made under this Policy after a Free Look cancellation notice has been submitted.
3. Lapse and Reinstatement

If the premium is not paid within the Grace Period, this Policy shall lapse and no benefit shall be payable. A lapsed Policy may be reinstated within twelve (12) months of the lapse date, subject to: (a) payment of all outstanding premiums with interest at the Company’s prevailing rate; (b) production of evidence of continued insurability satisfactory to the Company; and (c) payment of a reinstatement fee, if applicable. The Company reserves the right to decline reinstatement or to modify the terms of reinstatement. Reinstatement shall not be permitted after twelve (12) months from the lapse date.
4. Incontestability

After this Policy has been in force for a continuous period of two (2) years from the Commencement Date, the Company shall not contest its validity on the ground of misrepresentation or non-disclosure in the Proposal Form, except in the case of fraudulent misrepresentation or fraudulent non-disclosure. This incontestability clause does not apply to any Excluded Cause, which shall remain excluded regardless of the period for which the Policy has been in force.
5. Nomination of Beneficiary

The Policyholder may nominate one or more beneficiaries to receive the Sum Assured on the death of the Life Assured. A nomination made in the Policy Schedule or by written notice to the Company shall take effect from the date of receipt of the notice by the Company. The Policyholder may change the nomination at any time during the Policy Term by written notice to the Company. In the absence of a valid nomination, or where all nominated beneficiaries have predeceased the Life Assured, the Sum Assured shall be paid to the legal representative of the estate of the Life Assured.
6. Assignment

This Policy may be assigned as security for a loan or other obligation with the written consent of the Company. An assignment must be executed in writing and registered with the Company before it takes effect. An assigned Policy may not be further assigned without the prior written consent of the assignee. Assignment does not affect the Exclusions applicable to this Policy.
7. Dispute Resolution

Any dispute arising under or in connection with this Policy shall be referred in the first instance to the Company’s internal complaints resolution process. If the dispute is not resolved within forty-five (45) days of formal complaint, the Policyholder or claimant may refer the matter to the NAICOM Consumer Protection Bureau or to the courts of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. This Policy is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
EXCLUSIONS
No benefit is payable under this Policy if the death of the Life Assured is directly or indirectly caused by or arises out of any of the following:

items.h: Suicide or intentional self-inflicted injury, within twenty-four (24) months of the Commencement Date of this Policy or, where the Policy has been reinstated, within twenty-four (24) months of the date of reinstatement;
War (whether declared or undeclared), invasion, act of foreign enemy, civil war, rebellion, insurrection, or military coup, where the Life Assured is an active participant;
Participation in any criminal act or the commission of any indictable offence;

The use of or addiction to any prohibited substance under the Dangerous Drugs Act or any successor legislation, unless the substance was administered by or on the direction of a registered medical practitioner for legitimate medical treatment;
Aviation, other than as a fare-paying passenger on a scheduled commercial airline service.

blocks.h: Exclusions are among the most litigated provisions in life insurance. Key points for practitioners:

• Suicide exclusion: The 24-month suicide exclusion is standard in the Nigerian market to prevent adverse selection by individuals contemplating suicide. After 24 months, suicide is covered. This is a material fact the proposer need not disclose at application (it is a post-inception risk, not a pre-existing condition).

• Burden of proof: Under Leadway Assurance v. Zeco (2005), ambiguous exclusion clauses are construed contra proferentem — against the insurer. The insurer bears the burden of proving that a death falls within an exclusion.

• Aviation exclusion: The standard aviation exclusion covers the insured as crew or private pilot. The exception for scheduled commercial passenger flights is standard — routine air travel by an insured is not excluded. [Chapter 11]
CLAIMS PROCEDURE
On the death of the Life Assured, the nominated beneficiary or claimant shall:

items.h: Notify the Company of the death within twelve (12) months of the date of death, using the Company’s Claims Notification Form (see Document 2E in this Appendix) or by written notice to the Company’s registered office;

Submit to the Company: (a) the original Policy document; (b) a certified copy of the Death Certificate issued by the appropriate civil authority; (c) proof of identity of the claimant (government-issued ID); (d) the claimant’s bank account details for electronic payment; and (e) such additional evidence as the Company may reasonably require in the circumstances of the death;

The Company shall acknowledge receipt of the notification within five (5) business days and shall assess and settle all valid claims within sixty (60) days of notification of the claim, in accordance with the requirements of NIIRA 2025.

blocks.h: IN WITNESS WHEREOF this Policy has been executed on behalf of the Company.

blocks.h: For individual life assurance applications. Guidance notes explain the purpose of each section.
APEX LIFE INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED
INDIVIDUAL LIFE ASSURANCE PROPOSAL FORM

blocks.title: IMPORTANT NOTICE TO PROPOSER — DUTY OF DISCLOSURE

blocks.h: You are required by law and by the terms of this proposal to disclose to the Company all facts which are material to this proposal, whether or not questions relating to such facts appear in this form. A material fact is any information that would influence a prudent insurer in deciding whether to accept this proposal and on what terms. If you are in any doubt whether a fact is material, you should disclose it. Failure to disclose a material fact may entitle the Company to avoid the policy and refuse all claims. This disclosure obligation applies both at the time of application and, for any new application, at the time of reinstatement.
SECTION 1: PERSONAL DETAILS OF PROPOSER

The proposer is the person entering into the insurance contract with the insurer — the person who will own the policy and pay the premiums. In most individual life cases, the proposer and the life assured are the same person. Where they differ (e.g., a spouse insuring the other spouse), both sections 1 and 2 must be completed. NIN is required for KYC compliance under NIIRA 2025 and the MLPPA 2022.
SECTION 2: LIFE TO BE ASSURED (if different from proposer)

The life assured is the person on whose life the insurance is effected. Where the proposer and life assured are different people, the proposer must demonstrate an insurable interest in the life assured’s life at the time of application. In Nigerian law, a spouse has unlimited insurable interest in the other spouse’s life; a creditor has insurable interest up to the outstanding debt amount. [Chapter 11, Chief Omonuwa v. Insurance Company of Nigeria (1983)]
SECTION 3: BENEFIT SELECTION

Financial underwriting: For large sums assured, the insurer must assess whether the level of coverage is financially justified by the proposer’s income and assets. The rule of thumb is that a death benefit should not exceed 10–15× annual income without specific justification (e.g., a business loan of specific quantum). Over-insurance creates a moral hazard and is uninsurable in most markets including Nigeria. [Chapter 11]

blocks.h: SECTION 4: HEALTH DECLARATION

The health declaration is the most legally sensitive section of the proposal form. Every question must be answered fully and honestly. If you are unsure whether a past condition is relevant, answer YES and provide details — it is the underwriter’s job to assess relevance, not the proposer’s. Failure to disclose a health condition, even if the proposer believes it is trivial or cured, can void the policy if it is later found to be material.

If the sum assured exceeds the non-medical limit for the proposer’s age (as published in the insurer’s underwriting manual), additional medical evidence (blood tests, medical examination, specialist reports) will be required before the policy can be issued.

Very high aggregate coverage relative to income may indicate over-insurance or financial motivation. Disclosure of declined or postponed applications is essential — failure to disclose a previous decline is a serious non-disclosure that will typically entitle the insurer to void the policy.

blocks.h: The Free Cover Limit (FCL) is the maximum sum assured per member provided without individual medical underwriting. Every eligible employee is automatically covered up to the FCL from day one. Employees with benefit entitlements above the FCL require evidence of insurability (medical evidence). The FCL is set by the insurer based on the group size and demographic profile — larger, better-diversified groups qualify for higher FCLs. [Chapter 30]

The group premium rate of 0.43% of total annual emoluments is an experience-rated rate reflecting the group’s age/gender profile and past claims experience. A younger, healthier group will attract a lower rate. Group rates are reviewed at each renewal based on the year’s claims experience. [Chapter 30]
SELECTED CLAUSES
Clause 1: Eligibility

All persons in permanent employment with the Employer who have completed their probationary period (if any) shall be eligible for coverage under this Policy on the Commencement Date, or on the date they complete their probationary period, whichever is later. Temporary, contract, and agency workers engaged through a third-party employer are not eligible under this Policy. The Employer shall notify the Company in writing of any changes in eligible membership within thirty (30) days of the change.
Clause 2: Benefit Structure

On the death of an Eligible Employee while in active employment with the Employer and while this Policy is in force, the Company shall pay to the Employer a death benefit equal to three times (3×) the deceased employee’s Total Annual Emoluments at the date of death, subject to the Minimum and Maximum benefits specified in the Policy Schedule. Total Annual Emoluments includes basic salary plus all regular allowances (housing, transport, medical, utilities) but excludes discretionary bonuses, overtime, and reimbursed expenses.
Clause 3: Free Cover Limit and Evidence of Insurability

Every Eligible Employee is covered automatically for a death benefit up to the Free Cover Limit specified in the Policy Schedule without individual medical underwriting. An Eligible Employee whose benefit entitlement exceeds the Free Cover Limit must provide evidence of insurability satisfactory to the Company for the excess amount. The Company reserves the right to: (a) accept the excess at standard terms; (b) accept the excess subject to an additional premium; (c) accept the excess subject to a specific exclusion; or (d) decline to provide cover for the excess amount. The portion of the benefit up to the FCL remains in force regardless of the decision on the excess.
Clause 4: Employer’s Obligation to Pay Premium

The Employer shall pay the annual premium to the Company on or before the Commencement Date and on or before each Renewal Date. Non-payment of the annual premium shall entitle the Company to cancel this Policy with thirty (30) days’ written notice to the Employer. Where this Policy is cancelled for non-payment of premium, no benefit is payable in respect of any death occurring after the cancellation date. The Employer’s failure to maintain this Policy is an offence under Section 4 of the Pension Reform Act 2014 and may be reported by the Company to NAICOM and PenCom.
Clause 5: Annual Census

The Employer shall submit to the Company an updated census of all Eligible Employees within sixty (60) days of the Policy Renewal Date. The census shall include for each member: full name; date of birth; gender; job title; Total Annual Emoluments; and date of joining the scheme. The premium for the renewal year shall be calculated based on the census information. The Employer shall immediately notify the Company of any employee joining or leaving the scheme during the policy year.
Clause 6: Claims Procedure

On the death of an Eligible Employee, the Employer shall: (a) notify the Company in writing within thirty (30) days of the date of death; (b) submit the completed Claims Notification Form together with: a certified copy of the Death Certificate; evidence of the deceased’s employment and Total Annual Emoluments (payslip or letter from HR); the employee’s NIN and date of birth confirmation; and the beneficiary’s bank account details and government ID. The Company shall acknowledge receipt within five (5) business days and settle valid claims within sixty (60) days of notification of the claim. The death benefit shall be paid to the Employer, who shall distribute the benefit to the deceased’s nominated beneficiaries or estate as required by law.

In group life insurance, the insurer pays the death benefit to the employer (the policyholder), not directly to the deceased’s family. The employer is responsible for distributing the benefit to the nominated beneficiary or estate. Employers should maintain updated beneficiary nomination forms for all employees and should distribute benefits promptly — delayed distribution to bereaved families is a significant market conduct issue in the Nigerian market. [Chapter 30]

blocks.h: ANNUITY OPTIONS

Each option shows the monthly income that would be payable from the purchase price of ₦28,875,000. The income is guaranteed for life — it will never stop, regardless of how long the annuitant lives. blocks.h: A common question for retiring members: ‘At what age does the escalating annuity generate more total income than the level annuity?’

Conclusion: The escalating annuity overtakes the level annuity in total cumulative income at approximately Year 16 (age 76). An annuitant who lives beyond age 76 receives more total income from the escalating option. An annuitant who dies before age 76 receives more from the level option. The choice depends on the annuitant’s health status, life expectancy expectations, and need for inflation protection.
